extracted.intended_audience: Army public affairs officers (PAOs), commanders, unit PA staffs, and contracting/printing liaisons
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory guidance for producing, clearing, contracting, and releasing Army public affairs materials (including community/civilian enterprise newspapers, contingency releases, contractor materials, and internal information products). Covers what to include in printer briefings, Privacy Act release criteria, submission/clearance rules, masthead/disclaimer requirements, and PA program management controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare a briefing for potential printers
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a briefing for potential printers to sell the printer on the CE concept and explain 'what is in it for the CE printer.' Information should include, but not be limited to, the following items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sell the concept; explain benefits to the printer; include mission statement, market demographics, purchasing power, captive market/exclusive distribution, other market facts, and results of a resource study (see separate criteria for each specific item).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide a brief mission statement of the community/unit and the newspaper
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a brief mission statement of the community and/or unit and the newspaper. Explain how the newspaper meets the interests and needs of the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe purpose and audience alignment succinctly so the printer understands readership/mission fit and editorial responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide demographics (market) information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide demographic (market) information including military and civilian population, payrolls, grade demographics, children, local national employees, family members, and geographical dispersion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include: (1) military population by junior enlisted, senior enlisted, officers (including RC & retirees); (2) civilian population (GS & NAF); (3) total military payroll; (4) total civilian payroll; (5) grade demographics with monthly pay approximations for E‑1 to O‑4+ categories (round figures; do not calculate taxes/BAS); (6) number of children (use local school data if available); (7) local national employees and payroll if OCONUS; (8) number of family members and percent working/average income if possible; (9) geographic dispersion (approx numbers at each location).

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on purchasing power
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus the briefing on the audience's purchasing power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show advertisers/printers the market's ability to spend — payrolls, employment, family income, shopping/work/leisure patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize captive market and exclusive distribution access
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasize that the paper reaches a captive market and offers exclusive distribution access to the audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stress exclusivity of distribution channels and access to military/captive audiences as a selling point for profitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include other facts about the market
rubrics_metrics.description: Include any other facts about the market (for example, where people shop, work, live, and relax).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide contextual consumer-behavior data useful to printers and advertisers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct a resource study to define demographics and buying intentions
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct a resource study to define demographics and buying intentions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use surveys, local data, and studies to document market characteristics and advertiser potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify potential printers
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify potential printers through local Chambers of Commerce, business directories, local contracting office, PX, commissary, library, and clubs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check local publications, television guides, and other distributed media for printer names/addresses; compile a list of prospective printers for outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contacting printers — initial approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Contact printing representative by phone or, preferably, in person and indicate interest in meeting to discuss the possibility of the printer producing your newspaper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Face-to-face contact is preferred. Initial contact should be exploratory and set up a meeting; do not imply contractual commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document unsuccessful scheduling attempts
rubrics_metrics.description: If attempts to schedule a meeting are unsuccessful, forward documentation through PAO channels to the ACOM PAO including dates, times, and brief descriptions of each attempt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documented attempts are required because authorized funds may be used for printing only after it's shown that a CE newspaper is not feasible. Include specifics of outreach; follow PAO reporting lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting printing representative — state objective and avoid implying agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin meetings by informing the representative that the objective is seeking information; do not imply or lead them to believe you are obtaining an agreement during this meeting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make clear that specifications and official contacts, should they come, will be handled by the contracting office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation to printers — show product and comparative examples
rubrics_metrics.description: During the presentation, show the representative the newspaper and, if possible, obtain CE newspapers from other installations; explain differences between papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present demographics, profit potential, distribution possibilities; obtain case study info from other printers; be transparent about press run vs total population and do not conflate circulation with readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not mislead on circulation vs readership
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not mislead the printing representative into believing that the circulation figure represents readership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If press run is X but total population is larger, clarify what each number represents and discuss realistic potential for copies and distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss potential for growth and distribution channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Talk about potential with the CE (more copies, exclusive distribution) and local official distribution channels that can be used to distribute a CE newspaper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain realistic growth projections and how official distribution channels can augment reach; be careful presenting hypothetical gains as guarantees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bidding — provide bidder names to contracting office
rubrics_metrics.description: Tell interested representatives that their name, along with other prospective bidders, will be provided to the contracting office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not represent the contracting office; simply inform bidders their interest will be forwarded for formal procurement action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow contracting provisions for CE requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Commands will follow the provisions of this regulation for CE requirements for contracting; additional provisions may be added if not contradictory and realistic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate with contracting office and SJA; ensure additional specs are realistic to allow the civilian printer to succeed; changes may be negotiated in later years if performance warrants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Privacy Act scope — who is an 'individual' and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: The term individual applies only to living U.S. citizens or aliens admitted for permanent residence; rights of minors or incompetents may be exercised by parent/guardian; Privacy Act confers no rights on deceased persons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests are processed under both Privacy Act and FOIA; FOIA exemption 6 allows withholding to protect privacy of surviving family members when disclosure would disrupt their peace of mind (e.g., autopsy reports).

rubrics_metrics.name: Age or date of birth not routinely releasable
rubrics_metrics.description: Age or date of birth information is not routinely or normally releasable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate reasons for disclosure and balance against degree of personal privacy invasion before releasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Home of record and present address — case-by-case
rubrics_metrics.description: No general rule exists for disclosing home of record; requests are weighted case-by-case. Present location (city) may be provided but not street address; desires of individuals/next of kin should be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Home of record may usually be released if no street address is given; consent removes problems but objections do not necessarily control release — balance public interest vs privacy under FOIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marital status not routinely releasable
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual's marital status is not routinely or normally disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons for disclosure must be evaluated and balanced against privacy invasion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards and decorations/citations are releasable
rubrics_metrics.description: Award, decoration, and/or citation information is releasable and generally publicized in installation newspapers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most awards have visible tokens and are public events; such information is normally public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education, schooling, and specialty information generally releasable
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on major area of study, school, year of graduation, degree, and specialty designator is generally releasable under FOIA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Routine educational background details may be released unless other restrictions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Race usually not releasable unless relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: In most cases, an individual's race is not releasable because it may be an unwarranted privacy invasion; release when relevant to essential facts (e.g., racially oriented protest).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only release race information when it is material to the story or essential facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character of discharge — administrative vs punitive
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative discharge character is not releasable; discharge resulting from court-martial (punitive) is releasable because court-martial proceedings are public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not release indications of honorable/general/other-than-honorable administrative discharges without written consent; court-martial sentences and related public records may be released.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty status information is releasable
rubrics_metrics.description: Duty status information (e.g., unauthorized absence, desertion, hospitalization, confinement pending trial) is releasable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Release factual duty status items; coordinate with appropriate authorities when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel board decisions — group vs individual
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel board decision information is releasable after final approval if the board action applies to a category of persons; results affecting individuals are not generally releasable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results affecting groups (promotion boards, augmentation boards) are releasable; individual actions such as administrative discharge boards are typically confidential unless already public via individual/counsel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographs custody — generally releasable unless unwarranted privacy invasion
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs of DOD military and civilian personnel taken for official purposes are generally releasable unless they depict matters that would constitute a clearly unwarranted personal privacy invasion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award ceremony photos, selection file photos, chain-of-command photos are generally releasable; assess for privacy invasions before release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name/duty address of members in sensitive/routinely deployable/foreign-stationed units not routinely releasable
rubrics_metrics.description: The name and/or duty address of a member assigned to a sensitive, routinely deployable, or foreign-stationed unit is not routinely releasable due to security risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The releasing authority (normally the unit commander) must weigh public interest against privacy/security; Secretary of Defense (Public Affairs) is sole approving authority for releasing rosters listing such members by name.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protected health information requires consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Protected health information will not be released without the prior consent of the individual or their representative; consent is recorded on DA Form 4876.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Medical unit commanders are release authority for their commands; follow consent procedures strictly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractor submissions must follow FAR/AFARS and contract terms
rubrics_metrics.description: In prescribing procedures for submission, review, and clearance of industry-originated materials, the Department of the Army defers to Army/industry interface guidance in the FAR, AFARS, DFARS and contract terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These rules also apply to educational institutions and all phases of contracting (preaward, proposals, modifications, grants). Follow contract security and clearance provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not release procurement info on Army‑contracted R&D without prior approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Department of the Army agencies and contractors will not release procurement information on Army-contracted research and development projects without prior approval and clearance from ASA(ALT).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similarly, agencies or educational institutions must obtain prior approval/clearance. Classified/unclassified distinctions apply; consult contracting/security offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classified-contract handling and safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: A classified contract requires access to classified information to bid or perform; contractors are guided by security items in the contract and DD Form 254.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow DOD security regulations (DOD 5220.22-R/M, AR 380-49) for safeguarding and proposed release of information contractors may possess or access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submit unclassified contractor materials to designated PA office prior to publication
rubrics_metrics.description: When unclassified contracts do not give specific instructions on releasing information, contractors should submit informational materials prior to publication to a PA office designated by the administrative contracting officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voluntary submission is a business courtesy and helps prevent accidental release of inaccurate or classified information; submissions to other offices will be referred to the administrative contracting officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: PAOs act in advisory role for contractor-originated materials; originator retains final decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for materials developed under contract requirements, PAOs review voluntarily submitted materials in an advisory capacity; final decisions on accuracy, style, and good taste remain with the originator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAO recommendations should be taken seriously, but originators have ultimate control unless contractually constrained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific and technical information clearance limits
rubrics_metrics.description: PAOs do not have authority to clear scientific and technical information for public release but will assist proponents in determining clearance level; material that discloses classified military applications or would be adverse to national interest will not be released.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some material requires clearance through HQDA or OSD; export/ITAR restrictions may apply (DODD 5230.24/5230.25); prepare public scientific/technical releases under AR 70‑31 and forward to appropriate clearance authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission requirements — number and type of copies
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting material for clearance, submit the specified number and types of copies depending on medium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Written materials and still photographs—submit three copies (photos properly captioned) plus copies for intervening HQ record files. Scientific/technical papers and presentations—three copies including viewgraphs, charts, graphs. Fact sheets, pamphlets, brochures—three copies with full text, layout, and illustrative materials. Contractor advertisements—three copies including text, layout, artwork, photographs. Exhibits—three copies of design/layout and copy. Motion picture/videotape—submit preliminary concept (3 copies), final shooting script (3 copies), one rough cut minus soundtrack, and one print or copy of final narration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use model contingency releases and checklists for NBC incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: Use provided model PA checklists and sample contingency releases (Figures I‑1 through I‑9) for nuclear, biological, and chemical accidents and incidents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the sample release that matches the threat level (no danger, possible danger, probable danger) and adapt wording to incident specifics while following clearance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal materials should be localized and easy to use at unit level
rubrics_metrics.description: Materials developed at any level should be produced for easy use at the unit level and unit commanders should localize materials to meet command and audience needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor AF/DA products to local audiences; provide templates and guidance to enable unit-level adaptation without changing intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Department of Defense and Army common-use products and services
rubrics_metrics.description: AFIS provides common-use support materials (e.g., AFIS press pack); HQDA provides products and services (Army News Service, Soldiers Magazine, DAVIS, training workshops) to support PA objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAOs should use central resources, market stories to Army News Service, and send PA staff to yearly journalism workshops; use DAVIS and ArmyLINK/PA Link resources as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Masthead disclaimer required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: The masthead disclaimer must note: (a) the Army is an authorized publication and contents are not necessarily official views; (b) editorial content responsibility of the command PAO; (c) printed by (private firm) under exclusive contract; (d) appearance of advertising is not endorsement by U.S. Army; (e) advertised goods/services made available without regard to non-merit factors and violation leads to refusal to print ads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include all elements in the masthead disclaimer verbatim or close to ensure legal/ethical clarity; see sample masthead figure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Army newspaper/magazine masthead required listings
rubrics_metrics.description: Mastheads must list: (a) name of commanding officer and/or publishing authority; (b) name of the PAO; (c) names and editorial titles of staff assigned to prepare editorial content; (d) office addresses and telephone numbers of the editorial staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure masthead contains required organizational and contact information; CE guides and installation maps must include at least (a) (b) and (c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Management control: commanders develop PA guidance/strategies/plans/operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Have commanders developed PA guidance, strategies, plans, and operations?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a management control test item — document existence and evidence of implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management control: PAO assigned to commander's staff with direct access
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the PAO assigned to the commander's personal or special staff and has direct access to the commander?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm organizational placement and reporting lines that grant PAO requisite access for timely guidance and decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management control: PA offices managed by qualified PA personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Are PA offices, units, sections, and functions managed and supervised only by qualified PA personnel?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify qualifications, training, and assignment records for PA personnel responsible for release and program management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management control: information for release is accurate and devoid of propaganda
rubrics_metrics.description: Is all information intended for release through PA to internal and external audiences accurate and devoid of propaganda?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test for factual accuracy and adherence to policy/ethics; identify and correct propaganda or misleading content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management control: UPAR appointment when PAO not designated
rubrics_metrics.description: If not supported by a designated PAO, has an UPAR (unit public affairs representative) been appointed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm UPAR appointments and authority when a designated PAO is not present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management control: training program for UPARs
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there a training program in place for UPARs?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify training availability, curriculum, and attendance records for UPARs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management control: PA training program for leaders and Soldiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there a PA training program in place for leaders and Soldiers (non-PAO personnel)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for scoped training to inform leaders and Soldiers about media interaction, release policies, and communication responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management control: action to correct known erroneous public media information
rubrics_metrics.description: Has appropriate action been taken to correct any known erroneous information about the Army that appears in public media?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document corrective steps taken (requests for correction, press releases, follow-up), and evidence of outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management control: PAO designated as command web content manager
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the PAO designated as the command Web content manager for review and release of official information intended for public and command Web sites?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm formal designation and responsibilities to ensure web content compliance with AR 25‑1 and information release policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management control: quarterly review of publicly accessible Web sites
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the PAO conduct reviews of publicly accessible Web sites on a quarterly basis to ensure compliance with AR 25‑1 and content relevance?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure records of quarterly reviews and remediation actions exist to maintain policy compliance and relevance.
